items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

One afternoon Nila was returning from the market when she noticed a wallet beside a fruit stall. She picked it up and wondered what to do next.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A wallet near the market

One afternoon Nila was returning from the market when she noticed a wallet beside a fruit stall. She picked it up and wondered what to do next. She asked the stallkeeper whether he had seen anyone drop it. He had not noticed its owner. Nila opened the wallet only to look for identification. She found a card with a name but no telephone number. The stallkeeper suggested taking it to the nearby police desk. Nila agreed and gave the wallet to an officer. The officer recorded where she had found it. Later, a worried woman came to report a missing wallet. After checking her identity, the officer returned it to her. The woman thanked Nila for her honesty. Nila went home happy that the wallet was safely returned.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

A group of students wanted to grow vegetables behind their school. At first, they worked eagerly, but after a few weeks they stopped visiting the garden.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The neglected garden

A group of students wanted to grow vegetables behind their school. At first, they worked eagerly, but after a few weeks they stopped visiting the garden. One morning they found weeds growing around the young plants. Some leaves were drooping in the dry soil. The students realised that their plan needed regular care. They met their teacher and asked for advice. She encouraged them to share the work fairly. Together they made a weekly watering and weeding schedule. Each small team took responsibility for one day. They also collected rainwater in a covered container. After several weeks, the plants began to grow well again. The students harvested a few vegetables and shared them with the school cook. They learned that a good beginning must be followed by steady effort.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

On her way to school, Rupa saw that the small wooden bridge over a narrow ditch had been damaged by rain. Several younger children were waiting on the other side.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A broken bridge

On her way to school, Rupa saw that the small wooden bridge over a narrow ditch had been damaged by rain. Several younger children were waiting on the other side. Rupa told the children not to step onto the broken boards. She remembered a longer path that crossed the ditch at a safe culvert. She asked an adult nearby to accompany the group. Together they walked along the longer route to school. After arriving, Rupa informed the headteacher about the bridge. The headteacher contacted local residents and the relevant authorities. They placed a warning sign near the damaged crossing. A repair team inspected the bridge and replaced the unsafe boards. The adults checked the bridge before allowing children to use it again. The children were relieved to have a safe route. Rupa learned the value of careful action and asking adults for help.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

After school, Arif discovered a notebook on a bench at the bus stop. He noticed a name on its cover, but he did not know the owner.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Lost Notebook

After school, Arif discovered a notebook on a bench at the bus stop. He noticed a name on its cover, but he did not know the owner. He took the notebook to the school office. The clerk recognised the name as that of a student from another class. She contacted the class teacher. The teacher asked her students about the notebook. Soon the owner came to the office. She explained that she had left it while waiting for the bus. The clerk asked her to describe its cover. The description matched the notebook. She returned it to the relieved student. The student thanked Arif the next day. Arif was glad that he had taken the notebook to a safe place.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Mitu promised her grandmother that she would visit her on Friday. On that morning, her friends invited her to a football match.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A Promise Kept

Mitu promised her grandmother that she would visit her on Friday. On that morning, her friends invited her to a football match. Mitu wanted to watch the match very much. Then she remembered her promise. She explained the situation to her friends. They suggested that she visit her grandmother first. Mitu took some fruit and went to her grandmother’s house. Her grandmother was delighted to see her. They talked about the old days and shared the fruit. Mitu helped her arrange some books on a low shelf. When it was time to leave, her grandmother thanked her. Mitu reached the field before the second half began. She enjoyed both the visit and the game.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Tanvir left home late on the day of a school exhibition. When he reached the bus stop, the bus had already gone.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Missed Bus

Tanvir left home late on the day of a school exhibition. When he reached the bus stop, the bus had already gone. He felt worried because his model was needed at the exhibition. He called his teacher to explain the delay. The teacher told him to travel safely rather than rush. Tanvir checked the time of the next bus. It was due in fifteen minutes. He waited with his model protected inside a bag. When the bus arrived, he found a seat near the front. He reached school shortly after the exhibition began. His classmates had kept a space ready for his model. Tanvir set it up and explained it to the visitors. Afterwards, he decided to leave earlier for important events.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

For weeks, Lata and her friends had planned a picnic in the park. On the chosen morning, heavy rain began to fall.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Rainy-Day Plan

For weeks, Lata and her friends had planned a picnic in the park. On the chosen morning, heavy rain began to fall. The children were disappointed at first. Their teacher reminded them not to travel through flooded streets. They decided to postpone the picnic. Instead, each student prepared something at home for a later class meeting. Lata drew a picture of the park. One friend wrote a short poem about rain. Another made a list of games for the next sunny day. The teacher collected their ideas when school reopened. A week later, the weather improved. The class enjoyed the picnic safely. Their preparation made the new plan even more enjoyable.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Sadia found several extra bean seeds after planting her small garden. She wondered whether her neighbours could use them.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Seed Exchange

Sadia found several extra bean seeds after planting her small garden. She wondered whether her neighbours could use them. She put the seeds in clean paper packets. On each packet she wrote the name of the plant. She asked her mother to help her speak to the neighbours. Several families were interested in growing beans. One neighbour offered tomato seeds in exchange. Another shared advice about watering seedlings. Sadia planted a few tomato seeds in a pot. The neighbours compared their plants as they grew. When a seedling looked weak, they discussed what it needed. Soon the lane had several small gardens. Sadia learned that sharing resources can bring people together.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

During a class game, Rafi accidentally knocked over his friend’s water bottle. The water spilled across a poster they had made together.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A Careful Apology

During a class game, Rafi accidentally knocked over his friend’s water bottle. The water spilled across a poster they had made together. Rafi quickly moved the bottle away from the poster. His friend looked upset because the colours had run. Rafi admitted that he had been careless. He apologised without blaming anyone else. Together they lifted the poster onto a dry table. Their teacher brought paper towels to absorb the water. The picture could not be restored completely. Rafi offered to help make a new one. His friend agreed and suggested a simpler design. They worked together after class and finished it the next day. Their honest conversation helped protect their friendship.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The clock in the school library stopped one afternoon. Students began arriving late for their next lessons because they trusted its hands.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Library Clock

The clock in the school library stopped one afternoon. Students began arriving late for their next lessons because they trusted its hands. The librarian checked the battery first. She found that it had run out. She told the students that the clock was not working. A student wrote a temporary notice and placed it nearby. The librarian obtained a new battery from the office. Together with a staff member, she replaced the old one. They set the hands using a reliable clock. The next morning they checked that it still kept the correct time. The librarian removed the warning notice. She thanked the students for reporting the problem. Everyone returned to reading without worrying about a misleading clock.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Nabil was waiting outside school when a sudden shower began. He had an umbrella, but his neighbour Joya had none.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Shared Umbrella

Nabil was waiting outside school when a sudden shower began. He had an umbrella, but his neighbour Joya had none. Joya’s home was on the same street as Nabil’s. He offered to share the umbrella. They waited until the heaviest rain had passed. Then they walked slowly along the pavement. At a busy road, they stopped and used the marked crossing. The umbrella was small, so they stayed close together. When the wind grew stronger, they sheltered beside a shop. The shopkeeper told them a drain ahead had overflowed. They chose a safer route around it. Soon they reached Joya’s gate. Joya thanked Nabil, who then continued home.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

A new student named Farhan joined Class Eight in the middle of the term. During the first break, he sat alone at his desk.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Quiet New Student

A new student named Farhan joined Class Eight in the middle of the term. During the first break, he sat alone at his desk. A classmate named Rima noticed that he looked uncertain. She introduced herself and asked if he wanted to join her group. Farhan agreed, although he spoke quietly at first. The group showed him the library and the playground. They explained the timetable and the rules of their classroom. At lunch, Farhan shared a story about his old school. The others listened with interest. In a later lesson, he offered an idea for a group poster. His classmates included it in their design. By the end of the week, Farhan felt more comfortable. Rima learned that a simple invitation can help someone feel welcome.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The students noticed that a tap in the school washroom kept dripping. Every day a small pool of water formed underneath it.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Leaking Tap

The students noticed that a tap in the school washroom kept dripping. Every day a small pool of water formed underneath it. They told their class teacher about the leak. She asked the caretaker to inspect the tap. The caretaker placed a bucket underneath while waiting for a repair. The students used the collected water for cleaning where appropriate. The headteacher arranged for a plumber to visit. The plumber replaced a worn part inside the tap. He checked that the tap closed properly. The students cleared the floor so no one would slip. Their teacher discussed why leaks should be reported early. The class made a reminder about turning taps off carefully. The small repair prevented further waste.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Jerin entered a school drawing competition but did not win a prize. She folded her picture and said she would never draw again.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A Second Attempt

Jerin entered a school drawing competition but did not win a prize. She folded her picture and said she would never draw again. Her art teacher asked her what she liked about the picture. Jerin pointed to the colours in the sky. The teacher agreed that the colours were lively. She also suggested practising the shapes of trees. Jerin took the advice home. She spent a little time drawing different trees each week. Her younger brother offered to be her audience. Later, she entered another school activity. This time she enjoyed explaining how she had improved. Whether or not she won, she felt proud of her effort. She discovered that one disappointment need not end a favourite hobby.

items.text:
11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

A notice about a neighbourhood clean-up appeared on the school board. Many students wanted to join, but they did not know what to bring.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Community Notice

A notice about a neighbourhood clean-up appeared on the school board. Many students wanted to join, but they did not know what to bring. Their teacher contacted the organisers for details. The organisers asked volunteers to bring gloves and reusable water bottles. They also explained that adults would supervise the work. The students wrote the information on the class board. On the appointed morning, they met the adults at the community centre. The organisers divided them into small groups. Each group collected litter from a safe area. Sharp or dangerous objects were left for the adults to handle. The volunteers sorted the collected waste as instructed. They washed their hands after the work. The cleaner surroundings encouraged them to keep the area tidy.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Sohan borrowed a storybook from his friend Anika. One evening, he noticed that a page had come loose.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Borrowed Book

Sohan borrowed a storybook from his friend Anika. One evening, he noticed that a page had come loose. He remembered that the book belonged to Anika. He decided not to hide the damage. The next day he showed her the loose page and apologised. Anika appreciated his honesty but felt disappointed. They asked the school librarian how to handle the book. The librarian advised them not to use ordinary adhesive tape. She showed them how to keep the page safely inside a protective envelope. Sohan offered to help arrange a proper repair. With an adult’s help, they took the book to a local bookbinder. The bookbinder repaired the page. Sohan returned the book and thanked Anika for lending it.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The class was preparing a short play for an assembly. On rehearsal day, the student playing the narrator lost her voice.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Small Stage

The class was preparing a short play for an assembly. On rehearsal day, the student playing the narrator lost her voice. She told the teacher that she could not speak loudly. The teacher advised her to rest rather than strain her voice. The group discussed how to continue the rehearsal. Another student offered to read the narrator’s lines. The original narrator followed the script silently and helped with cues. The actors adjusted their movements to the new reader. At first, they missed several signals. They practised again and agreed on clear hand gestures. On assembly day, the narrator’s voice had improved. She and the substitute shared the reading. The play went well because everyone supported the change.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

After the final lesson, Rina could not find her lunchbox. She remembered placing it near the classroom window.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Missing Lunchbox

After the final lesson, Rina could not find her lunchbox. She remembered placing it near the classroom window. She checked her bag and the shelf under her desk. The lunchbox was not there. Her friend suggested asking the class monitor. The monitor had seen a similar box in the corridor. They went to the corridor together but found only a water bottle. A cleaner told them that a lunchbox had been taken to the office. Rina went there with her friend. She described its colour and the sticker on its lid. The office assistant checked the description and returned it. Rina thanked the cleaner and the assistant. She wrote her name on the box so it would be easier to identify.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

During a quiz, Imran gave an answer that made several classmates laugh. He became embarrassed and stopped raising his hand.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Wrong Answer

During a quiz, Imran gave an answer that made several classmates laugh. He became embarrassed and stopped raising his hand. The teacher reminded the class that mistakes are part of learning. She asked Imran to explain how he had reached his answer. He described the first step of his reasoning. The teacher showed him where the calculation had changed. Together they worked through the problem on the board. His classmates saw that the first step had been correct. One student apologised for laughing. Imran tried a similar question at home. The next day he volunteered an answer again. This time his reasoning led to the correct result. He felt more confident because he had learned from the mistake.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

A crowd gathered at the ferry terminal after a long delay. A young boy became separated from his family among the waiting passengers.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Ferry Queue

A crowd gathered at the ferry terminal after a long delay. A young boy became separated from his family among the waiting passengers. A shopkeeper noticed the boy looking worried. She asked him to stay beside her stall. She informed a terminal official about the situation. The official made an announcement describing where the boy could be found. The boy remembered his mother’s name and shared it with the official. Soon a woman approached the stall. She spoke to the official and identified her son. The boy recognised her and ran to her. The official checked that they were travelling together. The mother thanked the shopkeeper for helping safely. The family then joined the queue together.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The students had two ideas for a wall magazine: a nature issue and a sports issue. Both groups wanted their idea to be chosen.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Class Vote

The students had two ideas for a wall magazine: a nature issue and a sports issue. Both groups wanted their idea to be chosen. Their teacher suggested that each group explain its plan. The nature group proposed articles about local trees. The sports group suggested reports on school games. Other students asked questions about both plans. The class then held a secret vote. The nature issue received more votes. The sports group was disappointed but accepted the result. The teacher suggested making sports the theme of the next issue. Everyone helped collect and edit material for the first magazine. The finished pages included drawings, poems and short reports. The students learned that listening and fair voting can settle a disagreement.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Tisha’s bicycle chain came off while she was riding near home. She stopped safely beside the road and looked at it.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Repaired Bicycle

Tisha’s bicycle chain came off while she was riding near home. She stopped safely beside the road and looked at it. She knew that she should not continue riding with a loose chain. She called her father and explained where she was. He came with a neighbour who understood bicycle repairs. They walked the bicycle to a nearby repair shop. The mechanic checked the chain and gears. He found that the chain needed adjustment. He put it back and tested the pedals. He also checked the brakes and tyres. Tisha watched and asked how to notice a problem early. The mechanic explained some basic safety checks. Tisha thanked him and rode home only after the bicycle had been checked.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The school club received a box of coloured paper for a group project. When the box was opened, there was less paper than the students expected.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A Fair Share

The school club received a box of coloured paper for a group project. When the box was opened, there was less paper than the students expected. Several students reached for their favourite colours. Their leader asked everyone to pause and count the sheets. The group listed the materials each team needed. They discovered that some teams could use both sides of a sheet. Others agreed to combine smaller pieces into a collage. The leader divided the remaining paper as fairly as possible. A teacher gave them some clean scrap paper for practice. The teams avoided cutting the best sheets until their designs were ready. By the end of the session, every team had completed its work. A few unused sheets were saved for another day. The students saw that planning could make limited resources go further.

When the school meeting ended, Meena noticed a pair of spectacles under a chair. She looked around, but everyone had already left.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Found Spectacles

When the school meeting ended, Meena noticed a pair of spectacles under a chair. She looked around, but everyone had already left. She picked them up carefully. She asked the caretaker whether anyone had reported a loss. He suggested taking them to the office. The office assistant placed them in a labelled box. Later, a visitor came back looking for her spectacles. She described the frame and where she had been sitting. The assistant checked the description. The visitor received her spectacles. She was relieved to see them again. Meena met her outside the office. The visitor thanked her for her care.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

The science teacher asked students to observe rainfall for a week. Rakib’s group needed a simple way to record it.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Rain Gauge

The science teacher asked students to observe rainfall for a week. Rakib’s group needed a simple way to record it. They asked their teacher how to use a measuring container safely. She supplied a suitable clear container and a ruler. The group placed it in an open area with adult supervision. They checked that it would not easily fall over. Each morning they recorded the water level. They emptied the container after recording. They also wrote down the date. On one day there was no rain. They entered zero rather than leaving the record blank. At the end of the week they compared their results. Their chart showed how rainfall had varied.

Maya and her team were designing a poster about road safety. A power cut came just before they could print their pictures.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Unfinished Poster

Maya and her team were designing a poster about road safety. A power cut came just before they could print their pictures. The group looked at the materials on their table. They found paper, pencils and coloured markers. Maya suggested drawing the pictures by hand. One student sketched a pedestrian crossing. Another wrote a short safety message. A third drew a traffic light. They checked the spelling together. When the electricity returned, the poster was almost finished. They decided to keep their handmade design. The class displayed it near the entrance. The group was pleased that it had found another way to work.

An elderly neighbour gave Nuri a clay pot for her balcony plants. While moving it, she discovered a small crack near the base.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Clay Pot

An elderly neighbour gave Nuri a clay pot for her balcony plants. While moving it, she discovered a small crack near the base. Nuri did not want to throw the pot away immediately. She showed the crack to her mother. Her mother suggested asking a local potter for advice. The potter examined the pot. He explained that it was not suitable for holding water. He suggested using it as a dry container. Nuri cleaned and dried the pot. She used it to store empty seed packets. She placed it in a sheltered corner. The neighbour liked its new purpose. Nuri learned to consider a safe second use for old objects.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

One morning, Karim heard a knock at the door before breakfast. His cousin had arrived unexpectedly with a small bag.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Early Visitor

One morning, Karim heard a knock at the door before breakfast. His cousin had arrived unexpectedly with a small bag. Karim invited him inside. His cousin explained that his bus had reached town early. Karim’s mother welcomed him and offered him water. The family made room at the breakfast table. After breakfast, Karim showed his cousin a photo album. They found a picture from a family picnic. His cousin told a funny story about that day. Later, the family called to let the cousin’s parents know he had arrived safely. Karim helped him carry his bag to the guest room. They planned to visit the library together. The unexpected morning became a happy family memory.
items.page: Original fictional practice; model test Q11 format.

The school cricket team needed a captain for an upcoming friendly match. Two students wanted the role.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Team Captain

The school cricket team needed a captain for an upcoming friendly match. Two students wanted the role. The coach asked each candidate to explain how they would support the team. Both spoke about practising and encouraging others. The players then voted. Samir received more votes. The other candidate, Rashed, was disappointed. Samir thanked him for offering to help. He asked Rashed to organise the warm-up. Rashed accepted and suggested a practice routine. The team worked together during the match. They did not win, but they played fairly. Afterwards, the coach praised their cooperation.
items.page: Original fictional practice; model test Q11 format.

Sample title: The Broken Pencil

During an examination practice, Sumi’s pencil point broke. She realised that she had left her sharpener at home. She raised her hand to ask the teacher for help. The teacher reminded her to remain seated. A spare sharpener was available on the teacher’s desk. The teacher brought it to Sumi. Sumi sharpened her pencil carefully. She thanked the teacher and continued writing. She checked how much time was left. She completed the easier questions first. Then she returned to the more difficult ones. That evening she prepared her stationery for the next day. She learned to check her supplies in advance.

While watering a plant, Bithi saw a butterfly resting on a leaf. She wanted to show it to her younger brother.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Garden Visitor

While watering a plant, Bithi saw a butterfly resting on a leaf. She wanted to show it to her younger brother. She called him quietly from the doorway. He came without running towards the plant. They watched the butterfly open and close its wings. It moved to a nearby flower. Their father brought a small notebook. The children drew what they could see. They did not touch the butterfly. After a while, it flew over the wall. Bithi wrote down the date of the sighting. The children looked for a book about local butterflies. Their observation made them more curious about the garden.

The home economics group was preparing a fruit salad. Just before mixing the fruit, they noticed that they had forgotten the bananas.

Sample title: The Missing Ingredient

The home economics group was preparing a fruit salad. Just before mixing the fruit, they noticed that they had forgotten the bananas. Their teacher asked them to check what else was available. They had apples, guavas and ripe papaya. The teacher confirmed that these had been washed. One student cut the fruit under supervision. Another arranged clean bowls on the table. The group mixed the fruit carefully. They discussed how a recipe can be adjusted. Everyone received a portion. The group cleaned the utensils afterwards. They added bananas to the list for another day. Their salad was colourful even without the missing ingredient.

On a school trip, the class reached a museum with many rooms. The guide gave each group a map of the building.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Helpful Map

On a school trip, the class reached a museum with many rooms. The guide gave each group a map of the building. The teacher asked the groups to stay with their assigned adults. Zara studied the map with her friends. They identified the entrance and the meeting point. The guide showed them where the history gallery was located. The group walked there with their supervisor. They read the labels beside several exhibits. One student noticed a symbol for the stairs on the map. The group used the map to find the next gallery. Before leaving, they returned to the meeting point. The teacher counted the students. Everyone boarded the bus together.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

Rana received invitations to two family events on the same afternoon. Both were important to him, but the places were far apart.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Two Invitations

Rana received invitations to two family events on the same afternoon. Both were important to him, but the places were far apart. He discussed the times with his parents. They checked how long the journey would take. It was not possible to attend both events fully. Rana decided to visit the first gathering briefly. His parents called the second family to explain. They agreed on a suitable arrival time. Rana prepared small cards for both hosts. At the first event he greeted everyone and stayed for a short time. He then travelled with his parents to the second event. Both families understood his careful plan. Rana was glad he had communicated early.

11. Read the opening of the story below and complete it in at least ten new sentences. Give a suitable title to it.

While reading a story, Lami found a word she had never seen before. She could not understand the sentence around it.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Unfamiliar Word

While reading a story, Lami found a word she had never seen before. She could not understand the sentence around it. First, she read the whole paragraph again. She guessed that the word described a feeling. Then she looked it up in a dictionary. She found more than one meaning. She compared the meanings with the sentence. One meaning made sense in the story. She wrote it in her notebook. She also copied a short example of her own. The next day she asked her teacher to check it. The teacher confirmed her choice. Lami continued reading with a better understanding.

Before leaving for school, Hasan noticed that a button had fallen from his shirt. He had very little time before the bus arrived.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Missing Button

Before leaving for school, Hasan noticed that a button had fallen from his shirt. He had very little time before the bus arrived. He found the button on the floor. He placed it in a small box so it would not be lost. His mother helped him choose another clean shirt. Hasan caught the bus without rushing. After school, he asked his mother to show him how to sew a button. She brought a needle and thread. She explained how to handle the needle carefully. Hasan practised under her supervision. Together they attached the button securely. He put away the needle and thread. Hasan felt pleased to have learned a useful skill.

The leaves of the class plant began to turn yellow. Several students thought that it simply needed more water.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Classroom Plant

The leaves of the class plant began to turn yellow. Several students thought that it simply needed more water. Their teacher asked them to inspect the soil first. It was already very wet. They decided not to add more water immediately. The teacher helped them move the pot to a brighter place. They checked that the pot had drainage holes. For several days, they observed the plant without disturbing it. The soil gradually became less wet. New leaves appeared later. The students recorded what they had changed. They agreed to check the soil before watering. They learned that care begins with observation.

The music club was learning a song for a school event. At first, the group could not agree on the rhythm.
items.explanation:
Sample title: A Difficult Song

The music club was learning a song for a school event. At first, the group could not agree on the rhythm. The instructor asked them to listen to the melody again. She clapped the beat slowly. The students followed her without singing. Next, they practised one short section. A few students suggested marking the pauses in their notebooks. The group tried the same section again. Their timing improved with practice. They added the next section gradually. Before the event, they rehearsed the whole song together. On the day, they listened carefully to one another. Their patience helped them perform as a team.

After arriving at school, Faria realised that her completed assignment was still on her table at home. The teacher was about to collect the papers.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Forgotten Assignment

After arriving at school, Faria realised that her completed assignment was still on her table at home. The teacher was about to collect the papers. Faria explained the situation honestly to her teacher. She did not claim that she had already submitted it. The teacher asked when she could bring the work. Faria said she could bring it the next morning. The teacher noted the arrangement. At home, Faria placed the assignment inside her schoolbag. She also made a checklist for the following day. She arrived early and handed in the work. The teacher checked the date and accepted it according to the class rules. Faria thanked her for listening. The checklist helped her remember her materials afterwards.

A small kitten appeared near the school gate during lunch break. Several children gathered around it.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Stray Kitten

A small kitten appeared near the school gate during lunch break. Several children gathered around it. The teacher asked the children to give the kitten space. She checked that it was not blocking the gate. The caretaker brought a shallow bowl of water. An adult contacted a local animal welfare volunteer for advice. The volunteer asked whether the kitten had an owner nearby. The caretaker spoke to nearby shopkeepers. One shopkeeper recognised it as a neighbour’s kitten. The neighbour came and identified the kitten. She carried it home safely. The teacher reminded students not to handle unknown animals without adult guidance. The children were relieved that the kitten was reunited with its owner.

Before a school cultural day, the class planned a table showing traditional crafts. Everyone wanted to contribute something. The teacher asked students to bring only items their families agreed to lend. Rupa brought a small embroidered cloth. Saif brought a photograph of a clay pot. Another student prepared a label for each item. The group checked that the names were spelled correctly. They arranged the objects where visitors could see them safely. During the event, students explained what they knew about the crafts. When a visitor asked a difficult question, they admitted they were unsure. Their teacher helped them look for a reliable answer. After the event, each item was returned to its owner. The display encouraged the class to learn more about local traditions.

On Friday afternoon, the sports teacher could not find the key to the equipment cupboard. The class needed to put away the balls.

Sample title: The Missing Key

On Friday afternoon, the sports teacher could not find the key to the equipment cupboard. The class needed to put away the balls. The teacher asked the students to remain in the playground. She checked her pockets and her desk. A student remembered seeing a key ring near the attendance book. The teacher looked under the book. The key was there. She opened the cupboard and counted the equipment. The students returned the balls and bats to their places. The teacher locked the cupboard again. She placed the key on its usual hook. The class reviewed the storage routine. Everyone was ready to leave together.

Tania was chosen to read a poem aloud at an assembly. She was nervous because she had never spoken before a large audience.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Poetry Reading

Tania was chosen to read a poem aloud at an assembly. She was nervous because she had never spoken before a large audience. Her friend offered to listen to a practice reading. Tania read the poem slowly at home. Her friend suggested pausing at the ends of meaningful phrases. Tania marked a few pauses on her copy. The teacher reminded her to speak clearly rather than hurry. She practised standing where everyone could see her. On assembly day she took a deep breath. She looked at the first line and began. After a moment, her voice became steadier. The audience listened quietly until she finished. Tania felt proud that practice had helped her face her fear.

After a family picnic, Imtiaz noticed several empty wrappers near their mat. The family was preparing to leave.

Sample title: The Picnic Litter

After a family picnic, Imtiaz noticed several empty wrappers near their mat. The family was preparing to leave. He pointed the wrappers out to his sister. Together they checked which items belonged to their family. Their parents gave them a rubbish bag. They collected their own waste and a few safe pieces nearby. They left sharp objects for an adult to handle. They tied the bag securely. At the park exit, they found the appropriate bin. The family washed their hands before eating again. Imtiaz’s sister suggested bringing reusable containers next time. Their parents agreed. The family left the picnic place tidy.

Sample title: The Long Walk

A village student named Salma walked a long way to school each day. One morning her usual path was closed for repairs. She stopped to read the warning sign. A worker explained that the bridge was being repaired. Salma called her mother from a nearby shop with the shopkeeper’s permission. Her mother advised her to use the marked alternative path. Several other students were going the same way with an adult. Salma joined them. The route took longer than usual. The adult informed the school about the delay. Salma arrived safely and explained what had happened. After school, her family checked the repair notice. They planned the next morning’s journey accordingly.

Grandfather wanted to make a favourite family dish, but he could not find the recipe he had written down. His grandchildren offered to help. They searched the kitchen drawer together. One child found a notebook of old recipes. The needed page was not inside. Grandfather remembered that his sister also knew the dish. They called her and asked for the ingredients. She described the steps slowly. One grandchild wrote them down. Grandfather checked the list before cooking. The family prepared the dish together. They saved the new recipe in the notebook. Everyone enjoyed both the meal and the shared memory.

Sample title: The Book Fair Budget

The school book fair had many interesting books. Nusrat had a limited amount of money to spend. She first walked around and compared the prices. She found a science book and a collection of stories. Together they cost more than she had. She asked whether either book was available in the school library. The librarian said the story collection could be borrowed. Nusrat decided to buy the science book. She checked its price once more before paying. She saved the remaining money. The following week she borrowed the story collection. She enjoyed both books in different ways. Her planning helped her use her budget well.

Some students were concerned about crossing a busy road on their way to school. Their families met to discuss a safer routine.
items.explanation:
Sample title: The Walking Group

Some students were concerned about crossing a busy road on their way to school. Their families met to discuss a safer routine. The families looked at the available routes. They chose a crossing with a clear view of traffic. Two adults agreed to accompany a walking group. The students met at a fixed time each morning. They waited on the pavement until everyone was ready. The adults reminded them to follow crossing rules. The group walked together without pushing. When one adult could not attend, another family member helped. The families reviewed the routine after a week. They adjusted the meeting time to avoid rushing. The students felt more confident travelling together.

Sample title: The Missed Practice

A debate team was preparing for a competition. One member, Fahim, missed a practice because he was ill. His teammates first asked how he was feeling. The teacher reminded Fahim to rest. The team sent him a summary of the practice. It included their main points and speaking order. When Fahim returned, he read the notes. He asked questions about a point he did not understand. A teammate explained the evidence they had chosen. The group rehearsed once more together. They made a small change to include Fahim’s suggestion. At the competition, each member knew their role. The team was glad they had kept everyone informed.

Sample title: A Letter of Thanks

After a local nurse spoke to their class about hygiene, the students wanted to thank her. They decided to write a letter together. The class discussed what they had learned from the talk. One student wrote a first draft. Another checked the greeting and the nurse’s name. The group added a sentence about washing hands properly. They also thanked her for answering their questions. The teacher reviewed the letter for clarity. Several students signed it on behalf of the class. The school office sent it to the nurse. A few days later, the nurse replied with a kind message. The students placed her reply on the noticeboard. They were pleased that their thanks had reached her.
